structured.reason: The description contains defensive framing that reacts to complaints in the reviews (category 3), and an implied limitation (category 2). (1) "The sturdy construction means you can wear them daily without worrying about easy breakage" answers the reviews reporting clips that "Broke on second use" and "easily broken during use." Raising breakage to reassure against it is a backhanded response to a known complaint. (2) "the large size... gives you room... while the smaller size suits finer or shorter styles" implies the large size is not suited to finer hair, which responds to reviews saying the clips were "Way to big for my hair" and "Would be fine for thicker hair." (3) "Choose the size that matches your hair length and thickness" likewise reacts to the "too large" complaints and implies that the wrong size is a problem. Together these point to product weaknesses, so the description does not stay entirely positive.
